question: 친자관계에 관한 설명 중 which one is not correct? (다툼이 있는 경우 판례에 의함)
A: 당사자 사이에 there is no natural parent-child relationship 임을 확인한다는 내용이 포함되어 있는 조정이나 재판상 화해가 성립하더라도 it has no effect.
B: ｢민법｣ 제777조에서 정한 a relative라도 ｢민법｣ 제865조에서 정한 interested party에 해당하는 경우에만 친생자관계존부확인의 소의 plaintiff standing이 인정된다.
C: 피상속인 甲(女)의 공동상속인 乙과 丙이 이미 상속재산을 분할 또는 처분한 이후에 丁이 甲의 child임이 친생자관계 존재확인판결의 확정으로 명백히 밝혀진 경우, 인지의 retroactive effect limitation에 관한 ｢민법｣ 제860조 단서는 적용되지 아니하므로 乙과 丙이 한 분할 또는 처분의 효력을 丁이 deny할 수 없다.
D: 정상적으로 혼인생활을 하고 있는 부부 사이에서 artificial insemination child가 출생하는 경우 인공수정으로 출생한 자녀는 남편의 child로 presumed되고, 남편이 인공수정에 consent하였다가 나중에 이를 revoke하고 친생부인의 소를 제기하는 것은 allowed되지 않는다.
E: 성전환자의 fundamental rights protection과 미성년 자녀의 protection 및 welfare와의 harmony를 이룰 수 있도록 legal interest balancing을 위한 여러 circumstances를 고려하여 substantively 판단하지 아니한 채 단지 성전환자에게 미성년 자녀가 있다는 사정만을 이유로 gender correction을 불허하여서는 아니 된다.

1. Summary of the case and issues
가. Summary of the case
Non-party 1(1909. 8. 10. 사망)은 2010. 8. 15. 건국훈장 4등급 애국장 포상대상자로 designated되었다. Non-party 1의 장녀 Non-party 2(사망)의 child인 Non-party 3이 administrative litigation을 통해 구 독립유공자예우에 관한 법률(2012. 2. 17. 법률 제11332호로 amended되기 전의 것, 이하 "구 독립유공자예우법"이라 한다)에 따른 독립유공자의 유족으로 recognized되자, Non-party 1의 장남 Non-party 4(사망)의 손자인 Plaintiff가 the Prosecutor를 상대로 Non-party 1과 Non-party 2 사이에 친생자관계가 존재하지 않는다는 confirmation을 구하는 등의 this action을 제기하였다.
The lower court는 Plaintiff가 위와 같은 친생자관계부존재확인판결을 받더라도 구 독립유공자예우법이 정한 기준에 따른 독립유공자의 유족으로 registered될 수 없고, 달리 친생자관계부존재확인을 구할 이해관계가 없다는 reason으로 plaintiff standing을 부정하고 this action을 dismissed하였다. 이에 대해 Plaintiff는 자신이 Non-party 1과 민법 제777조의 친족관계에 있으므로, prior Supreme Court precedents에 따라 당연히 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 interest가 있다고 주장하면서 appealed하였다.

나. Issue in this case
The issue in this case는 whether Plaintiff가 Non-party 1과 친족관계에 있다는 fact만으로 당연히 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있는지 여부이다. Issue에 관한 판단을 위해 first 민법 제865조에 의한 친생자관계존부확인의 소의 plaintiff standing 범위를 살펴보고, 민법 제777조에서 정한 친족은 그와 같은 status relation에 있다는 fact만으로 당연히 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있다고 한 prior Supreme Court precedent를 maintain할 것인지 examine하기로 한다.

2. 민법 제865조에 의한 친생자관계존부확인의 소의 원고적격
가. 친생자관계존부확인의 소의 제기권자
Parent-child relationship인 친자관계는 blood ties에 기초한 친생자관계와 당사자의 intent에 기초한 양친자관계로 divided된다. 그중 친생자관계에 관하여 Civil Act는 임신과 출산이라는 natural facts에 의하여 그 relationship이 clearly determined되는 모자관계와 달리 부자관계의 establishment과 dissolution에 대하여 several provisions를 두고 있다. 아내가 혼인 중에 임신한 child를 남편의 child로 presumed하는 친생추정 규정(제844조 제1항)과 이에 대한 rebuttal method인 친생부인의 소에 관한 provisions(제846조 내지 제851조), 재혼한 여자가 해산한 경우 법원에 의한 부의 결정에 관한 provision(제845조), 혼인외 출생자의 인지에 관한 provisions(제855조 제1항, 제863조), 인지의 취소 및 인지에 대한 이의의 소에 관한 provisions(제861조 및 제862조)이 이에 해당한다. 따라서 legal 친생자관계의 establishment과 dissolution을 구하는 litigation procedure에서는 위 각 provision에 expressly specified된 제소권자가 해당 provision이 정한 요건을 갖춰 소를 제기하는 것이 principle이다.
민법 제865조 제1항(이하 "이 사건 조항"이라 한다)은 "제845조, 제846조, 제848조, 제850조, 제851조, 제862조, 제863조의 규정에 의하여 소를 제기할 수 있는 자는 다른 사유를 원인으로 하여 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있다."라고 정한다. 이는 legal parent-child relation과 family relation register에 표시된 parent-child relation이 mismatch할 때 이를 correct하기 위하여 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있도록 한 것이다.
이 사건 조항이 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있는 자를 specific하게 특정하여 directly 규정하는 대신 litigation purpose가 similar한 다른 litigation procedure에 관한 provisions를 cite하면서 각 소의 제기권자에게 plaintiff standing을 부여하고 그 cause only를 달리하게 한 점을 보면, 이 사건 조항이 정한 친생자관계존부확인의 소는 legal 친생자관계의 establishment과 dissolution에 관한 other litigation procedure에 대하여 supplementary nature를 가진다.
이처럼 the form, wording, and structure of the provision, 위 각 규정들이 정한 litigation procedure의 특징, 친생자관계존부확인의 소의 supplementary nature 등을 consider하면, 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있는 자는 이 사건 조항에서 정한 제소권자로 limited된다고 봄이 proper하다.

나. 원고적격의 구체적 범위
(1) 친생자관계의 당사자로서 부, 모, 자녀
친생자관계의 party인 부, 모, 자녀는 이 사건 조항에 enumerated된 민법 제845조, 제846조, 제862조, 제863조에 의하여 소를 제기할 수 있는 자로서 다른 사유를 원인으로 하는 경우에는 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있다.

(2) 자녀의 직계비속과 그 법정대리인
친생자관계의 party인 자녀의 직계비속과 그 legal representative는 이 사건 조항에 enumerated된 민법 제863조에 의하여 소를 제기할 수 있는 자로서 다른 사유를 원인으로 하는 경우에는 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있다.

(3) 성년후견인, 유언집행자, 부(夫) 또는 처(妻)의 직계존속이나 직계비속
이 사건 조항에 enumerated된 민법 제848조, 제850조, 제851조는 모두 친생부인의 소의 plaintiff standing에 관한 basic provision인 민법 제846조를 premise로 하여 supplementary하게 plaintiff standing을 expand하는 provisions이다. 따라서 민법 제848조, 제850조, 제851조의 제소권자인 성년후견인, 유언집행자, 부 또는 처의 직계존속이나 직계비속은 위 provisions에 의하여 소를 제기할 수 있는 requirements를 갖춘 경우에 only plaintiff standing이 있다고 봄이 옳다. 즉, 성년후견인은 남편이나 아내가 성년후견을 받게 되었을 때(제848조), 유언집행자는 부 또는 처가 유언으로 친생자관계를 부정하는 intent를 표시한 때(제850조), 부 또는 처의 직계존속이나 직계비속은 부(夫)가 자녀의 출생 전에 사망하거나 부 또는 처가 친생부인의 소의 filing period 내에 사망한 때(제851조) 비로소 다른 사유를 원인으로 하여 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있다. 이들이 위와 같은 requirements를 충족하지 못한 경우에는 위 각 provisions에 의하여 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 plaintiff standing이 당연히 있다고 할 수 없다.

(4) 이해관계인
An interested person may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship on another ground pursuant to Civil Act Article 862, which is listed in the provision at issue. Here, 이해관계인 means a third party who has a legal interest, such as obtaining certain rights or being relieved from obligations, by a final judgment stating that a natural parent-child relationship exists or does not exist between other persons. Accordingly, only where the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship between other persons will, by judicial determination, have a concrete impact on the interested person’s own rights or obligations concerning inheritance, support, or the like, or on his or her legal status, may such person file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship as an interested person.
가족관계등록부상으로는 no kinship relation이 나타나지 않더라도 스스로 자녀의 생부 또는 생모라고 주장하면서 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기한 person은 그 judgment result에 따라 당사자와의 친생자관계 자체에 directly 영향을 받게 되므로 interested persons에 included된다.
결국 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기한 Plaintiff가 앞서 (1), (2), (3)에서 본 바와 같이 당연히 plaintiff standing이 recognized되는 경우가 아니라면, 여기서 말하는 interested person에 해당하는 경우에만 plaintiff standing이 있다. 이러한 interested person에 해당하는지 여부는 Plaintiff의 주장내용과 변론에 나타난 제반사정을 바탕으로 상속이나 부양 등에 관한 Plaintiff의 rights or obligations, legal status에 미치는 concrete impact가 무엇인지를 individually examine하여 판단해야 한다.

3. 민법 제777조에서 정한 친족은 당연히 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있는지 여부
가. 종전 대법원 판례
대법원 1981. 10. 13. 선고 80므60 전원합의체 판결은 구 인사소송법(1961. 12. 6. 법률 제803호로 enacted되어 1962. 1. 1.부터 시행되었고 1990. 12. 31. 법률 제4300호로 repealed되었다. 이하 같다) 제35조가 "당사자 및 법정대리인 또는 민법 제777조의 규정에 의한 친족은 언제든지 혼인무효의 소를 제기할 수 있다."라고 규정한 제26조를 민법 제865조에서 정한 친생자관계존부확인의 소에 준용하고 있음을 reason으로, 민법 제777조에서 정한 친족관계에 있다는 fact만으로 당연히 친생자관계존부확인의 소의 plaintiff standing이 인정된다고 하였다.
그 후 대법원은 구 인사소송법이 적용되는 case(대법원 1983. 3. 8. 선고 81므77 판결, 대법원 1991. 5. 28. 선고 90므347 판결 등 참조)에 대해서는 물론, 구 인사소송법이 repealed되면서 새로 enacted된 가사소송법(1990. 12. 31. 법률 제4300호로 enacted되어 1991. 1. 1.부터 시행되었다. 이하 같다)의 적용을 받는 case(대법원 1998. 10. 20. 선고 97므1585 판결, 대법원 2004. 2. 12. 선고 2003므2503 판결 등 참조)에 대해서도 같은 취지로 판단하였다.

나. 판례변경의 필요성
However, in light of the repeal of the former Act on Personal Status Litigation and other statutes, the enactment and implementation of the Family Litigation Act, family system changes such as the abolition of the head-of-family system, the special characteristics of status litigation, the diversification of family composition and respect for the parties’ intent in that regard, and balance with other litigation procedures aimed at the establishment or dissolution of a legal natural parent-child relationship, it must be concluded that the prior Supreme Court precedents holding that an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship may necessarily be filed merely on the ground that one is kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777 can no longer be maintained. The detailed reasons are as follows.
(1) The former Act on Personal Status Litigation, which set special provisions regarding litigation procedures concerning personal status in relation to the Civil Procedure Act, the basic Act governing ordinary civil litigation procedures, contained an express provision(Articles 35 and 26) stating that kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777 may necessarily file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship. In fact, this became the core basis of the prior Supreme Court precedents. However, unlike the former Act on Personal Status Litigation, the Family Litigation Act, which integrated the former Act on Personal Status Litigation and the former Family Affairs Adjudication Act(1963. 7. 31. 법률 제1375호로 enacted되어 1963. 10. 1.부터 시행되다가 1990. 12. 31. 법률 제4300호로 repealed되었다), contains no provision at all concerning who may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship. The Family Litigation Act merely applies mutatis mutandis the provisions concerning the opposing party in an action for nullity of marriage, etc.(Article 24) to an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, while not applying the provision concerning the person entitled to file suit(Article 23). Accordingly, with the repeal of the former Act on Personal Status Litigation and the implementation of the Family Litigation Act, the legal basis of the prior Supreme Court precedents disappeared.
(2) As legal norms surrounding family relations and social circumstances changed, social perceptions regarding natural parent-child relationships, which together with marital relations form the foundation of family relations, also changed.
At the time of the enactment of the Civil Act and even after the repeal of the former Act on Personal Status Litigation and the enactment of the Family Litigation Act, for a considerable period Korean civil law maintained the household head system, under which family relations were publicly recorded in the family register organized by household unit based on the head of family. At that time, most persons in a kinship relationship, such as the lineal ascendants and lineal descendants of the head of family, collateral relatives, and their spouses, were entered in the family register as members of the household centered on the head of family. However, with the 2005 amendment to the Civil Act, the household head system was completely abolished and reorganized into a family system centered on spouses and children, and as of January 1, 2008, when the Act on the Registration, etc. of Family Relations(2007. 5. 17. 법률 제8435호로 enacted; 이하 "가족관계등록법"이라 한다) came into force, the family relations registration register replacing the family register has recorded, centered on the individual, the occurrence and changes of family relations through marriage, birth, and the like. In addition, in our society, the nuclear family consisting of parents and unmarried children has already become the norm, rather than the traditional extended family, and with the progress of urbanization and industrialization, individualism and liberalism have become widely prevalent in family life as well.
In light of these legal and social changes concerning the family system and the like, unlike the period when the household head system was maintained, the legal and social basis for viewing kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777 as having a close status-related legal interest has weakened today.
(3) The action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is a litigation procedure designed to correct entries in the family relations registration register that do not correspond to the true blood relationship(가족관계등록법 Article 107). However, today family relations are formed not only on the basis of blood relations but also diversely on the basis of the parties’ intent. The Supreme Court has held that the presumption of legitimacy also applies to a child born through artificial insemination during marriage, and that even if it is revealed that a child conceived and born by a wife during marriage has no blood relationship with the husband, it cannot be said that the presumption of legitimacy does not apply(see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2016므2510 rendered on October 23, 2019). The Supreme Court has also held that where a party registers a child as born of the party’s own biological child with the intent to create an adoptive parent-child relationship, the effect of adoption is recognized if the requirements for adoption are satisfied(however, the Civil Act amended by Act No. 11300 on February 10, 2012 and effective as of July 1, 2013 requires approval from the Family Court as a requirement for adoption of a minor), and that a claim for confirmation of the nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is not permitted in relation thereto(see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2000므1493 rendered on May 24, 2001). This is because legal protection is needed not only where the presumption of legitimacy applies to a parent-child relationship formed without a blood relationship, but also where, even if the presumption of legitimacy does not apply, that parent-child relationship has been substantially formed on the basis of the parties’ intent. Accordingly, while respecting the free intent of the parties regarding the formation of the legal parent-child relationship that underlies marriage and family relations, it is necessary to impose certain limitations so that third parties do not improperly intervene in that regard.
(4) An action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship falls under a "Category A family litigation case" under the Family Litigation Act(Article 2, paragraph (1), subparagraph 1(a)). The effect of a judgment granting such an action extends to third parties as well(Article 21 of the same Act), and the court must investigate facts and take necessary evidence ex officio and may examine the parties at any time(Article 17 of the same Act). In particular, considering the reality that blood relationship can now be proved relatively easily through DNA testing and the like, broadly viewing the scope of third parties who may contest the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship in the name of finding the truth of blood ties and allowing the case to proceed to the merits is highly likely to inevitably undermine the stability of status order and infringe the parties’ autonomous decision-making regarding marriage and family life. Accordingly, it is not desirable to expand arbitrarily, by interpretation and without an express statutory basis, the scope of third parties who may bring an action contesting the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship.
Although the Family Litigation Act provides in Article 24, paragraph (2), and Article 28 for cases in which a third party files an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, these are provisions concerning the opposing party(defendant capacity), not the person entitled to sue, and therefore cannot serve as a basis for expanding the scope of persons entitled to file suit.
(5) Since an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is supplementary to other litigation procedures aimed at the establishment or dissolution of a legal natural parent-child relationship, it is clear that where such an action may be filed under another litigation procedure, an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is not permitted.
Meanwhile, where there is a dispute concerning a legal natural parent-child relationship, an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is often used in place of other litigation procedures whose filing requirements are relatively strict, and current practice also shows such a tendency. The Supreme Court has extended the legal principles concerning an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship to adoptive parent-child relationships as well(see Supreme Court Decision 92므372 rendered on July 16, 1993), and moreover, the filing period for an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is not prescribed except where one or both parties to the natural parent-child relationship have died(Civil Act Article 865, paragraph (2)).
In this way, the filing requirements for an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship have already been relaxed in several respects, and further expanding the scope of standing as Plaintiff to kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777 is not balanced even when compared with the other litigation procedures described above. This is even more so because of the risk that the action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship may be distorted into a means of circumventing the requirements or restrictions established by statutory provisions concerning other litigation procedures.
(6) The natural parent-child relationship, which forms the basis of status relationships, does not end merely as a matter between the parties, but may affect inheritance issues among relatives and various other legal relationships based on kinship, such as parental authority and support(see Supreme Court Decision 2004므405 rendered on June 24, 2004). It is therefore of course necessary that certain third parties also be given the opportunity to contest the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship through a proper judicial procedure. Since the Civil Act, in the provision at issue, allows a third party who is not a party to the natural parent-child relationship to contest its existence or nonexistence if that third party qualifies as an interested person, a third party who is kin also has standing if that person qualifies as an interested person. Accordingly, even if not all kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777 are uniformly granted standing as Plaintiff, it cannot be said that the rights or right to a judicial remedy of third parties who have a legal interest in the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship are unjustly restricted.

다. 판례의 변경
Accordingly, Supreme Court Decision 97므1585 rendered on October 20, 1998, which held in relation to cases governed by the Family Litigation Act that kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777, absent special circumstances, have a litigation interest in filing an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship merely by reason of being in such a status relationship, and Supreme Court Decision 2003므2503 rendered on February 12, 2004, and other judgments to the same effect, are changed to the extent they are inconsistent with the view of this judgment.

4. Determination in this case
가. According to the reasons of the lower court judgment, the following facts may be found.
(1) Non-party 1 was designated on 2010. 8. 15. as a recipient candidate for the Patriotic Medal, Grade 4, of the Order of Merit for National Foundation, and Non-party 1’s children were the eldest son Non-party 4, the eldest daughter Non-party 2, and the second daughter Non-party 5. Non-party 4 and his spouse and children, as well as Non-party 5 and her spouse, all died before the date on which the recipient candidate was designated, and the only surviving child of Non-party 5 was Non-party 6(date of birth omitted, male). Plaintiff is the grandson of Non-party 4.
(2) On 2010. 8. 30., Non-party 6 applied to the Gwangju Regional Office of Patriots and Veterans Affairs for registration as a bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence under Article 6 of the former Independence Merit Treatment Act, on the ground that he is a grandson of Non-party 1, and was registered on 2011. 11. 24. as the first-priority bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence.
(3) Meanwhile, Non-party 3(date of birth omitted, female) applied on 2011. 11. 25. to the Gwangju Regional Office of Patriots and Veterans Affairs for registration as a bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence, asserting that she is a child of Non-party 1’s eldest daughter Non-party 2, and thus the first in priority among Non-party 1’s grandchildren, but the head of the Gwangju Regional Office of Patriots and Veterans Affairs rejected the application on 2011. 11. 30. Thereafter, Non-party 3 filed an action for cancellation of the refusal to register her as a person of distinguished service to independence against the head of the Gwangju Regional Office of Patriots and Veterans Affairs(Gwangju District Court Case No. 2011구합4510), obtained a judgment in her favor on all claims, and that judgment later became final and conclusive after appeal and further appeal.

나. 위와 같은 factual relations을 앞서 본 legal principles에 비추어 살펴보면 다음과 같이 판단할 수 있다.
(1) Plaintiff는 Non-party 1의 lineal descendant(증손자)로 Non-party 1과 친족관계에 있지만, 이 사건 조항에 따라 당연히 plaintiff standing이 인정되는 person에 해당하지 않는다.
(2) According to Article 5, paragraph (1), and Article 12, paragraph (2), paragraph (4), subparagraph 1 of the former Independence Merit Treatment Act, compensation is paid only to one first-priority bereaved family member among the person of distinguished service to independence and his or her bereaved family members, and the scope of bereaved family members entitled to receive compensation is limited in the order of spouse, child, grandchild, and daughter-in-law of the person of distinguished service to independence, with the older person receiving priority if there are two or more persons of the same rank. Therefore, under the standards prescribed by the former Independence Merit Treatment Act, the Plaintiff, who is merely the great-grandchild of Non-party 1, cannot be registered as a bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence, and since Non-party 6 in addition to Non-party 3(child of the eldest daughter, Non-party 2) appears to be alive as a grandchild of Non-party 1, the Plaintiff cannot be registered as a bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence even if he obtains a judgment confirming the nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship between Non-party 1 and Non-party 2. Nor does the question whether the Plaintiff may be registered as a bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence depend on whether Non-party 2 is the child of Non-party 7, the wife of Non-party 1.
(3) Even if a judgment confirming that no natural parent-child relationship exists between Non-party 1 and Non-party 2, and between Non-party 7 and Non-party 2, respectively, becomes final and conclusive, Plaintiff cannot be said to have a legal interest therein. Accordingly, this action must be regarded as unlawful because it was filed by a person lacking plaintiff standing.

다. The lower court’s determination to the same effect is proper as it follows the legal principles discussed above. The lower court did not err, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, by misapprehending the law on plaintiff standing in an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, by failing to conduct the necessary examination, or by exceeding the bounds of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the principles of logic and experience.

5. Conclusion
The Plaintiff’s appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party; accordingly, judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition. Except for the separate opinion of Justice Ahn Cheol-sang and Justice Min Yoo-sook, the views of the participating Justices were unanimous, and there are supplementary opinions by Justice Park Jeong-hwa, Justice Kim Seon-su, and Justice Roh Jeong-hee regarding the majority opinion.

6. Separate opinion of Justice Ahn Cheol-sang and Justice Min Yoo-sook
We agree with the majority opinion regarding the change in Supreme Court precedent. However, we differ from the majority opinion as to the scope of persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship and whether the Plaintiff in this case falls within that category.

가. First, our view regarding the change in precedent.
(1) The provision at issue states, “A person who may institute an action pursuant to the provisions of Article 845, Article 846, Article 848, Article 850, Article 851, Article 862, or Article 863 may institute an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship on another ground.” Accordingly, it is clear from the wording of the provision at issue that the person entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is limited to the persons specified therein.
However, the former Act on Personal Status Litigation provided that “kin under Civil Act Article 777” may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship(Articles 26 and 35). Yet, since the provision at issue in the Civil Act had already expressly specified the person entitled to sue with respect to an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, the former Act on Personal Status Litigation’s inclusion of a separate provision concerning the person entitled to sue created systemic confusion. On 1990. 12. 31., the former Act on Personal Status Litigation and the former Family Affairs Adjudication Act were both repealed and the integrated Family Litigation Act came into force, and the Family Litigation Act deleted the provision from the former Act on Personal Status Litigation concerning the person entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship. With the implementation of the Family Litigation Act, the overlapping provisions were eliminated, and the persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship became governed solely by the provision at issue in the Civil Act.
(2) Supreme Court Decision 97므1585 rendered on 1998. 10. 20., which the majority opinion cites as a precedent to be changed, held that if a person is kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777, that person may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship merely by reason of being in such a status relationship, and thus failed properly to reflect the changes brought about by the repeal of the former Act on Personal Status Litigation and the implementation of the Family Litigation Act. However, Supreme Court Decision 2003므2503 rendered on 2004. 2. 12., also cited as a precedent to be changed, unlike Supreme Court Decision 97므1585, held that kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777 may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship as an "interested person" who is a person entitled to sue under the provision at issue. Accordingly, if one takes the later Supreme Court Decision 2003므2503 as the benchmark, the current Supreme Court precedent is not that kin under Civil Act Article 777 "become persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship even though there is no longer any legal basis"(the premise of the majority opinion), but rather that they "become persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship as interested persons under the provision at issue."
(3) Although the Civil Act as amended by Act No. 4199 on 1990. 1. 13. reduced the scope of kin, Supreme Court Decision 2003므2503, which held that kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777 necessarily fall within the category of "interested persons," may still be evaluated as merely following the repealed provisions of the former Act on Personal Status Litigation, and it is therefore appropriate to change it. Accordingly, the change in precedent should target the holding that "kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777 fall within the category of interested persons under the provision at issue merely by virtue of their status relationship," and we agree with the majority opinion as to such change in precedent.

나. In this case, the issue is whether the Plaintiff, as the great-grandchild of Non-party 1, falls within the persons entitled to sue under the provision at issue, namely "lineal descendants of the husband or wife" or "interested persons." Since we differ from the majority opinion on this point, we set forth our view in detail below.
(1) Before addressing the issue, we first consider the majority opinion concerning the necessity of changing precedent.
(a) According to the majority opinion, because family relations today are formed diversely not only on the basis of blood relations but also on the basis of the parties’ intent, the free intent of the parties should also be respected as to the existence or nonexistence of a legal natural parent-child relationship. However, an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is a judicial procedure for confirming the existence or nonexistence of a true blood relationship, and the existence or nonexistence of the legal natural parent-child relationship that is the subject matter of the litigation is not of a nature that can be determined by the free intent of the parties.
Under the Civil Act, the chapter on kin(Part IV) is broadly structured around Chapter 3, "Marriage," and Chapter 4, "Parents and Child," and Chapter 4, "Parents and Child," is again divided into provisions concerning Section 1, "Natural Child," and Section 2, "Adopted Child." This shows that the relationship between parents and children is formed on the basis of blood ties and the parties’ intent, but that among them the natural parent-child relationship is based on blood ties(the Supreme Court en banc Decision 2000므1493 rendered on 2001. 5. 24., cited by the majority opinion, concerns the legal doctrine of adoption, under which the parent-child relationship is formed by the parties’ intent).
In addition, in an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, admission of the claim and confession are not permitted(Article 12 of the Family Litigation Act), and the prior mediation principle also does not apply(Article 50, paragraph (1) of the same Act), so it is impossible in such proceedings to determine the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship by the parties’ intent. Disposition by the parties’ free will concerning the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is not permitted.
(b) The majority opinion takes the view that the scope of persons entitled to sue should be limited so that third parties do not improperly intervene in family relations. We fully agree that private life and domestic peace should be protected against threats by third parties. Indeed, Supreme Court en banc Decision 2016므2510 rendered on 2019. 10. 23. held, in substance, that in a natural parent-child relationship to which the presumption of legitimacy applies, third parties must be prevented from intervening indirectly in another person’s family matters by allowing only an action for disavowal of paternity, which strictly limits the persons entitled to sue and the filing period.
However, the action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship in this case is fundamentally different from an action for disavowal of paternity in this respect. Because a natural parent-child relationship to which the presumption of legitimacy applies can be denied only by a judgment in an action for disavowal of paternity, there is practical benefit in limiting the persons entitled to sue in order to achieve that purpose. By contrast, a natural parent-child relationship to which the presumption of legitimacy does not apply may not only be contested through an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, but when it becomes a preliminary issue in other litigation procedures such as civil litigation, anyone may allege and prove its nonexistence in that litigation procedure(see Supreme Court Decision 78다71 rendered on 1978. 4. 11.). Therefore, even if the scope of third parties who may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is limited, such limitation cannot prevent them from contesting the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship through civil litigation, etc. Limiting the scope of persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, as in the majority opinion, has little practical effect in preventing third parties from intervening in another person’s family matters and cannot be said to be an appropriate method. Rather, permitting certain third parties to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship makes it possible to finally resolve disputes surrounding status relationships and thereby also ensure the accuracy and authenticity of the family relations registration register. This is because only when the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is determined in the "disposition" of a judgment by filing an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship can the family relations registration register be corrected, the effect of a judgment granting the claim extends to third parties as well, and special provisions such as orders to undergo testing are more helpful in ascertaining the true blood relationship.
Even in this case, Non-party 3, a relative whose interests are opposed to those of the Plaintiff, had already, through administrative litigation, asserted that there is a natural parent-child relationship between her mother and Non-party 1, obtained a final and conclusive judgment in her favor, and the reasons for that judgment include a determination regarding blood relationship. It does not appear easy to preserve the peace of these families merely by blocking the Plaintiff’s filing of this subsequent action.
(c) Looking at the statistics on "litigation relating to parent-child relationships" in the Judicial Yearbook published annually by the courts over the past five years, actions for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship account for 75 to 80 percent of all litigation relating to parent-child relationships, occupying an overwhelming share. In actions for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, the rate at which the Plaintiff’s claim is granted at first instance exceeds 75 percent, and the appeal rate is only around 1 percent. Unlike the fact that an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is prescribed under the Civil Act as a supplementary form of litigation, in practice it has become the principal form of litigation relating to parent-child relationships, and although the Family Litigation Act is structured to have an adversarial-party framework, in practice there are mostly not serious disputes between the relevant parties concerning the very "existence or nonexistence of blood relationship."
Even today, as in the past when public registers, etc. for publicizing status relationships were not adequately established, birth registrations and the like are often made contrary to the actual blood relationship due to legal restrictions or personal circumstances. Under the Supreme Court precedents that a family relations registration register cannot be corrected absent a final and conclusive judgment concerning matters that have a significant impact under the law of kinship or inheritance, as prescribed in Article 2, paragraphs (1) and (2) of the Family Litigation Act(see the Supreme Court en banc Decision on correction of family registers, 93스14, 15, 16 rendered on 1993. 5. 22.), even if there is no substantive dispute between the parties regarding the "existence or nonexistence of blood relationship," an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, which is a family litigation with an adversarial structure, must nonetheless be filed in order to correct the family relations registration register(see the above statistics on the rate at which claims are granted and the appeal rate).
Furthermore, whether a person falls within the category of persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is a matter of standing as Plaintiff, which is a litigation requirement, and thus a matter to be examined ex officio. The more strictly the scope of standing as Plaintiff is limited or the more complex the criteria for judgment are set, the more likely it is, as noted above, that even where there is no substantive dispute between the parties regarding the existence or nonexistence of blood relationship, the court will ex officio examine standing as Plaintiff and dismiss the action, resulting in an increased number of such cases.
(d) The majority opinion is concerned that if the scope of persons entitled to sue is broadened, an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship may be distorted into a means of evading legal restrictions. However, that is a matter for the family court handling the case to faithfully examine the relevant issues and distinguish the genuine from the spurious; it is not a matter to be resolved by limiting standing as Plaintiff and thereby blocking the filing of the action itself.
(2) We now consider the first issue, namely the part of the majority opinion that limited the filing requirements for "lineal ascendants or lineal descendants of the husband or wife."
(a) The majority opinion states that "lineal ascendants or lineal descendants of the husband or wife" may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship only where the husband dies before the child’s birth or the husband or wife dies within the filing period for an action for disavowal of paternity.
However, because an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is a litigation procedure entirely different from an action for disavowal of paternity in terms of litigation structure and legal nature, it is not appropriate to require separate conditions, as in an action for disavowal of paternity, even when lineal ascendants or lineal descendants of the husband or wife file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship.
(b) An action for disavowal of paternity may be filed only by one of the spouses, and therefore it is necessary to make provision for the case where the person entitled to file it has died. Civil Act Article 851 provides that in such a case, the "lineal ascendants or lineal descendants" of the husband or wife may file the action. However, an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship expressly contemplates, from the outset, filing not only by the parties to the natural parent-child relationship but also by third parties(Article 24, paragraph (2), and Article 28 of the Family Litigation Act). Therefore, the structure in which, if the party entitled to file an action for disavowal of paternity dies, his or her lineal ascendants or lineal descendants become supplementary persons entitled to sue does not fit an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship.
An example will clarify this. Since the mother-child relationship arises from the natural facts of conception and birth, the wife(hereinafter "A") may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship against a person recorded in the family relations registration register as her biological child(hereinafter "B"), alleging the nonexistence of a blood relationship without any time limit, and if A dies, A’s lineal descendants may file such an action against B. In such a case, the majority opinion says that A’s lineal descendants may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship only if A died within the filing period for an action for disavowal of paternity(two years from the date on which the cause for disavowal was known). However, since there is no room for the presumption of legitimacy itself to arise between A and B, it is impossible to assume a date on which the cause for disavowal became known, and the filing period for an action for disavowal of paternity cannot run either. According to the majority opinion, it is difficult to tell how one is to determine whether the requirement of the filing-period limitation has been met. Moreover, while A could have filed the action at any time during her lifetime, once A dies, one arrives at the strange conclusion that, retroactively to some specific point in the past, the filing period had already expired.
(c) The parties to a natural parent-child relationship are the parent and the child. The lineal descendants of the child may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship pursuant to the provision at issue and Civil Act Article 863 without satisfying any other filing requirements, and the majority opinion does not differ on this point.
If the lineal descendants of the child are allowed to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship without any further restriction, it is balanced and natural in terms of textual interpretation to regard the lineal descendants of the parent as likewise being able to file such an action without any time limit. In practice, there is much greater possibility or necessity for the lineal descendants of the parent to file an action contesting the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship after the parent’s death than there is for the lineal descendants of the child to do so after the child’s death.
(d) In addition, where the parent, who is a party to the natural parent-child relationship, dies without filing an action for confirmation of the nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, and only a testamentary executor is appointed, or where adult guardianship has commenced while the parent had not filed such an action, the adult guardian and testamentary executor, as persons entitled to sue, will have the question of whether filing is permitted separately determined under the Civil Act provisions concerning the scope of their duties even if standing as Plaintiff is recognized under the provision at issue, and thus the issue differs from the present case.
(e) The reasons why descendants file an action after the parent has not, during the parent’s lifetime, resolved the family relations registration register so that it matches the blood relationship vary depending on individual circumstances and family relations. There may be cases in which a child files an action against the parent’s wishes during the parent’s lifetime, but as in the Judicial Yearbook statistics mentioned above, in most cases the first-instance judgment in favor of the Plaintiff is accepted by both sides and becomes final and conclusive as rendered. There are even cases where a person who, because there was no blood relationship and thus no substantive status as a child during the parent’s lifetime, claims inheritance rights on the basis of the family relations registration register after the parent’s death, causing other heirs to bring litigation.
(3) We now consider the second issue, namely the part of the majority opinion that explained the requirements for an "interested person."
(a) The majority opinion states that an "interested person," as a person entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, is a third party having a legal interest, such as obtaining certain rights or being relieved from obligations, by a final judgment confirming the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship between other persons. The majority opinion’s view on this point is almost identical to the holdings in Supreme Court Decision 4293민상314 rendered on 1960. 9. 29., and Supreme Court Decision 90므88 rendered on 1990. 7. 13., so it is in effect understood as relying on those decisions. However, because all of those Supreme Court decisions were holdings in cases governed by the already repealed former Act on Personal Status Litigation, it is not appropriate for the majority opinion to continue to rely on them.
(b) The primary criterion for determining the scope of an interested person should be whether the person suffers detriment in his or her legal status based on a status relationship due to the registration of a natural parent-child relationship different from the true blood relationship in the current family relations registration register, and whether there exists a legally protectable interest worth correcting through a judgment confirming the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship. The criterion presented by the majority opinion, namely whether the person "obtains certain rights or is relieved from obligations," is not an appropriate criterion because it may be extended to cases where there is no effect on status relationships but only a property interest(for example, an insurance beneficiary or a creditor of an heir).
(c) If whether a person qualifies as an interested person is to be determined case by case on the basis of the circumstances shown in the Plaintiff’s allegations or pleadings, there is a risk of a side effect whereby the focus of the family court’s examination and determination shifts from the "existence or nonexistence of blood relationship," which is the subject matter of the litigation, to the "impact on rights, obligations, or legal status." This is because, in litigation procedures in which the court must determine the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, the Plaintiff’s order of succession or order of support must first be alleged and examined in order to determine standing as Plaintiff.
Such side effects are more pronounced where the legal interest is related to public law status. The "impact on the rights and obligations of third parties" may appear, as in this case, in the form of public-law legal relationships where special statutes, including the former Independence Merit Treatment Act, provide for payment of compensation or benefits to a certain range of "bereaved family members," etc. In such cases, if the above principle is applied in determining whether a person qualifies as an interested person, the family court will bear the burden of ex officio examining and determining the compensation standards, the beneficiaries of benefits, and the scope of bereaved family members prescribed by various administrative statutes. It cannot be said to be appropriate to compel interpretation and determination of administrative statutes, which are not within the family court’s area of expertise, in a family litigation case.
In fact, before determining the "existence or nonexistence of blood relationship," which was the cause of action, the lower court in this case examined in detail the standards prescribed by the former Independence Merit Treatment Act and whether the Plaintiff could be registered as a bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence. It is not desirable for such examination and determination of administrative statutes to become the center of an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, which is a family litigation case.

다. In conclusion, we consider this case.
(1) Since the Plaintiff is a lineal descendant of Non-party 1 and Non-party 7, namely a great-grandchild, he falls under "lineal descendants of the husband or wife," which is a person entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship under the provision at issue and Civil Act Article 851. Moreover, whether the Plaintiff may be registered as a bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence under the former Independence Merit Treatment Act is not something to be strictly examined and determined ex officio, and once it is shown that the result of this case is likely to affect whether he may be registered as a bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence, he should be included among the persons entitled to sue as an interested person. Nevertheless, the lower court erred in its legal interpretation concerning standing as Plaintiff in an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship by failing to determine at all whether the Plaintiff, as a lineal descendant of Non-party 1, falls within the category of persons entitled to sue, and by holding that he lacked standing because he could not be registered as a bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence under the former Independence Merit Treatment Act.
(2) However, the lower court, as an alternative determination, found that the evidence was insufficient to conclude that no natural parent-child relationship exists between Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 and between Non-party 7 and Non-party 2, and instead recognized that such natural parent-child relationships exist in light of the various circumstances. This falls within the exclusive province of the lower court as the trier of fact, and it does not appear to contain any error exceeding the bounds of free evaluation of evidence. If so, even if this action is deemed lawful, the Plaintiff’s claim cannot be granted. Moreover, in this case, where only the Plaintiff appealed, setting aside the lower court judgment and dismissing the claim would result in a disadvantage to the Plaintiff; therefore, under the principle prohibiting reformatio in peius, the appeal has no choice but to be dismissed.
As stated above, although we agree with the majority opinion as to the conclusion of the case, because the reasons differ, we state this in a separate opinion.

7. Supplementary opinion of Justice Park Jeong-hwa, Justice Kim Seon-su, and Justice Roh Jeong-hee regarding the majority opinion
We offer supplementary reasoning to the majority opinion on several points.

가. The majority opinion stated that among the "adult guardian, testamentary executor, or lineal ascendants or lineal descendants of the husband or wife" listed in Civil Act Articles 848, 850, and 851, which are cited in the provision at issue, only those who satisfy the requirements for filing suit under those provisions have standing as Plaintiff, and that standing as Plaintiff is not necessarily recognized where those requirements are not met. This is reasonable for the following reasons.
(1) The provision at issue does not directly regulate who the persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship are. The provision at issue merely states that "a person who may institute an action pursuant to the provisions" listed therein may institute an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship on another ground. Accordingly, in light of the form, wording, and structure of the provision at issue, it is natural to interpret the persons who may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship as "persons who may file suit by satisfying the requirements under each provision" listed in the provision at issue.
(2) The requirements set forth in Civil Act Articles 848, 850, and 851 all pertain not to the grounds of an action for disavowal of paternity but to the "person entitled to sue." Accordingly, the requirements concerning the "person entitled to sue" under those provisions should also apply to the persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship.
(3) Since Civil Act Articles 848, 850, and 851, which are cited in the provision at issue, are all supplementary provisions concerning the person entitled to file an action for disavowal of paternity, the interpretive standard for determining "persons who may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship pursuant to those provisions" must be consistent. In other words, in the case of a testamentary executor under Civil Act Article 850, it should be interpreted that the executor may file an action for disavowal of paternity only when the husband or wife expresses by will an intent of denial, and that, pursuant to the provision at issue and Civil Act Article 850, the testamentary executor may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship only when the husband or wife has indicated by will an intent to deny the natural parent-child relationship. There is neither need nor reason to recognize standing as Plaintiff for a testamentary executor where there was no such will by the husband or wife.
(4) The separate opinion states that "lineal ascendants or lineal descendants of the husband or wife" under the provision at issue and Civil Act Article 851 may, without needing to satisfy the requirements set forth in those provisions, file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship without restriction. Civil Act Article 851 does not automatically allow the lineal ascendants or lineal descendants of the husband or wife to file an action for disavowal of paternity merely because the husband or wife has died; rather, it limits the filing period to cases where the husband dies before the child’s birth or where the husband or wife dies within the period for exercising the right of disavowal of paternity. This reflects the purpose of respecting the lifetime intent of the parties regarding the natural parent-child relationship and promoting stability in status order by permitting, exceptionally, persons other than the party entitled to disavow paternity(lineal ascendants or lineal descendants) to file an action for disavowal of paternity where the husband or wife had no opportunity during life even to file such an action or died before the period for exercising the right of disavowal expired and thus could not realize that intent.
However, if, as in the separate opinion, "lineal ascendants or lineal descendants of the husband or wife" may file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship without any restriction under the provision at issue, the result may be to undermine the purpose of Civil Act Article 851, which exceptionally allows persons who are not entitled to disavow paternity to file an action for disavowal of paternity only in limited cases. As the majority opinion explains, a natural parent-child relationship can be formed diversely not only on the basis of blood relations but also on the basis of the parties’ intent, and the presumption of legitimacy may also apply to a parent-child relationship formed without a blood relationship. However, where the parties to such a parent-child relationship formed without blood relation(especially the parent) die and a considerable amount of time passes, it may become difficult to objectively determine whether the person recorded as a child in the family relations registration register is a person to whom the presumption of legitimacy applies. In such cases, "lineal ascendants or lineal descendants of the husband or wife," who originally could not file an action for disavowal of paternity due to the restrictions in Civil Act Article 851, may nonetheless contest the existence or nonexistence of the blood relationship against the intent of the parties by filing an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship. Furthermore, where a parent-child relationship formed without blood relation is substantially formed on the basis of the parties’ intent, as in cases where a child born through artificial insemination is registered as a biological child even though the presumption of legitimacy does not apply, or where a child born out of wedlock of a spouse is registered as a biological child while satisfying the requirements and intent to adopt(the Civil Act as amended in 2012 and effective as of July 1, 2013 requires approval from the Family Court when adopting a minor, but the supplementary provisions limit retroactive effect), legal protection should not be excluded merely because the presumption of legitimacy does not apply. Even where the parent did not raise any issue during his or her lifetime regarding the existence or nonexistence of blood relation with the child, allowing the parent’s lineal ascendants or other lineal descendants to seek confirmation of the nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship against the child on the ground that there was no blood relation after the parent’s death may infringe the personality rights or right to pursue happiness of the parties concerning the formation of family relations. Accordingly, the separate opinion’s view that an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship may be filed without restriction merely because one is a lineal ascendant or lineal descendant of the husband or wife is not appropriate.
(5) The majority opinion’s interpretation, which narrows as much as possible the scope of persons whose standing as Plaintiff is necessarily recognized under the provision at issue, is not unrelated to the fact that the provision at issue designates interested persons as persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship. Even if standing as Plaintiff is not necessarily recognized under the provision at issue, an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship may still be filed where the person qualifies as an interested person; therefore, it is appropriate to interpret the scope of automatic persons entitled to sue under the provision at issue as above.

나. We now consider the standard for determining the scope of an interested person.
(1) The persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship under the provision at issue include interested persons. Because an interested person is a broad concept meaning a third party with a legal interest in the existence or nonexistence of another person’s natural parent-child relationship, it is important in practice to determine its specific scope. The majority opinion limits interested persons to those whose rights, obligations, or legal status concerning inheritance, support, or the like are concretely affected by the final and conclusive judgment on the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship. By contrast, the separate opinion states that in order to have standing as Plaintiff as an interested person, the person must have an interest worthy of legal protection to correct the record in the family relations registration register, and that this should be based on whether the person suffers detriment in legal status grounded in a status relationship due to a record in the family relations registration register contrary to the true blood relationship. However, the respective standards proposed by the majority opinion and the separate opinion do not in practice create a significant difference in determining whether a person is an interested person. This is because, even under the majority opinion, one examines what concrete effect exists on the person’s rights, obligations, or legal status concerning inheritance, support, or the like, and therefore, contrary to the concern expressed in the separate opinion, a third party who has no effect on status relationships and only a property interest will not be included among interested persons. In fact, it is difficult to find cases in prior Supreme Court precedents or lower court practice in which such a person was recognized as an interested person.
(2) The separate opinion points out that if the issue of whether a person qualifies as an interested person is to be determined individually in each case, there is a side effect whereby the focus of the family court’s examination and determination shifts from the subject matter of the litigation, namely the "existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship," to the Plaintiff’s "rights, obligations, or impact on legal status," or that the family court will bear the burden of having to interpret and determine administrative statutes.
However, since the provision at issue expressly designates interested persons as persons entitled to file an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, where the Plaintiff asserts that he or she filed such an action as an interested person, a stage must be gone through to determine whether the Plaintiff actually qualifies as such. Such review of party capacity also has practical value in harmoniously realizing the two ideas governing parent-child relationships, namely securing the legal stability of parent-child relationships and the principle of blood truth. Moreover, the need to reasonably adjust the scope of party capacity and establish criteria for such determination before proceeding to the merits is not a problem unique to family litigation cases. Today, family litigation cases often raise legal issues from other areas, including public law relations, but this is an unavoidable result of the very diverse and complex manner in which legal interests surrounding status relationships are manifested. Accordingly, the side effects pointed out by the separate opinion are not matters that must essentially be considered in determining the scope of interested persons and the principles for examining and deciding that issue.

As stated above, we present this supplementary opinion regarding the majority opinion."}

{"[2016MEU2510]": "The grounds for appeal를 판단한다.
1. Judgment on the grounds for appeal as to Defendant 1
가. 아내가 혼인 중 artificial insemination으로 임신하여 출산한 child의 친자관계
(1) whether the presumption of paternity provision applies to an artificial insemination child
민법은 부모와 자녀의 parent-child relationship 성립에 관하여 blood ties에 기초한 natural child relationship(제844조 이하에서 친생자에 관한 provisions을 두고 있다)과 parties’ intent에 기초한 adoptive relationship(제866조 이하에서 양자에 관한 provisions을 두고 있다)로 구분하고 있다. 이 중 natural parent-child relationship은 출생에 의하여 발생하는 parent-child relationship로서, 부모가 natural sexual intercourse로 임신한 child를 출산한 경우를 전제로 하므로 부모와 출생한 child 사이에는 biological blood relationship이 존재하는 것이 원칙이다.
친생자관계에서도 mother-child relationship과 father-child relationship은 different 모습으로 나타난다. 임신과 출산이라는 natural fact에 의하여 그 relationship이 clearly 결정되는 mother-child relationship과 달리, father-child relationship은 그 relationship 확정을 위한 separate requisites가 필요하다. 민법은 혼인 중에 아내가 임신한 child를 husband’s child로 presum e하는 presumption of paternity provision(제844조 제1항. 이하 ‘presumption of paternity provision’이라 한다)을 두고 있다. 혼인외 출생자의 경우에는 biological father가 acknowledge하거나(제855조 제1항) child가 father를 상대로 action for acknowledgment를 제기하여(제863조) natural parent-child relationship의 existence를 확정하는 방법으로 legal parent-child relationship을 창설할 수 있는데, 이때 father와 child 사이에 blood relationship이 존재하는지가 증명의 대상이 되는 main fact를 구성한다(대법원 2002. 6. 14. 선고 2001므1537 판결, 대법원 2015. 6. 11. 선고 2014므8217 판결 등 참조).
피고 1에 대한 이 사건 claim의 issue는 아내가 혼인 중 husband가 아닌 third party의 sperm를 제공받아 natural means가 아닌 artificial insemination으로 임신한 child(이하 ‘artificial insemination child’라 한다)를 출산한 경우 출생한 child의 parent-child relationship을 어떤 standard로 인정해야 하는가이다. 현행 민법에는 artificial insemination child의 parent-child relationship 성립에 관해서 express provision이 없다. 1958. 2. 22. 민법 제정 당시에는 아내가 artificial insemination으로 child를 임신할 수 있다는 possibility를 상정하지 못하였기 때문에 이에 관한 규정을 둘 수 없었다.
그러나 친생자와 관련된 Civil Act provisions, especially the presumption of paternity provision의 text and structure, 민법이 혼인 중 출생한 child의 legal status에 관하여 presumption of paternity provision을 두고 있는 basic legislative purpose and history, 그리고 Constitution이 보장하고 있는 marriage and family system에 비추어 보면, 아내가 혼인 중 husband가 아닌 third party의 sperm를 제공받아 artificial insemination으로 child를 출산한 경우에도 presumption of paternity provision을 적용하여 artificial insemination으로 출생한 child가 husband’s child로 presumed된다고 보는 것이 타당하다. detailed reasons는 다음과 같다.
(가) 먼저 presumption of paternity provision의 meaning에 관하여 본다.
Mother-child relationship은 birth라는 fact에 의하여 parent-child relationship이 성립하는 so-called natural parent-child relationship인 반면, father-child relationship은 natural fact의 existence를 알 수 없어 법률이 인정하는 경우에만 parent-child relationship이 성립한다는 의미에서 legal parent-child relationship이다. presumption of paternity provision은 아내가 혼인 중에 임신한 child를 출산한 경우 그 child를 husband’s natural child로 presume하고 있다. 나아가 민법은 혼인 중의 conception fact를 직접 증명하는 것이 쉽지 않다는 점을 고려하여 혼인이 성립한 날부터 200일 후 또는 혼인관계가 종료된 날부터 300일 이내에 출생한 child는 혼인 중에 임신한 것으로 presume하여(제844조 제2항, 제3항) uniform criteria에 따라 혼인 중 임신 여부를 정할 수 있도록 하였다. 이러한 presumption of paternity provision은 parent-child relationship의 scientific verification이 practically impossible하고 legal marital relationship에 있는 wife가 husband’s child를 conceive할 것이라는 social and legal background를 기초로 혼인 중 출생한 child가 husband와 blood relationship이 있을 probability가 높다는 것을 전제로 하고 있다.
presumption of paternity provision은 그 자체로 true blood relationship과 not correspond하는 legal parent-child relationship을 발생시킬 가능성을 내포하고 있다. 법률상 친자관계를 진실한 blood relationship에 부합시킬 수 있도록 하는 것이 Constitution이 보장하고 있는 marriage and family system의 principle이라고 볼 수 있으므로(헌법재판소 1997. 3. 27. 선고 95헌가14, 96헌가7 전원재판부 결정 등 참조), 이를 위해 민법은 presumption of paternity provision에 따라 형성된 father-child relationship을 제거할 수 있는 means로서 right to deny paternity를 husband와 wife에게 인정하고 있다(제847조. 이하 ‘provision on the action for disavowal of paternity’라 한다). 그러나 the period to exercise the right to disavow paternity를 too long 인정하거나 그 period를 제한하지 않으면 child’s status relation을 promptly determine해야 할 need와 status relations 주변 legal relations의 stability를 해칠 수 있으므로, 민법은 action for disavowal of paternity는 husband 또는 wife가 cause for disavowal of paternity를 알게 된 날부터 2년 내에 제기하여야 한다는 filing period를 정하고 있다(제847조 제1항). 이와 같이 standing과 filing period를 제한하는 provision on the action for disavowal of paternity에 따라 presumption of paternity의 effect는 법률에서 인정하는 other presumptions보다 stronger force를 갖는다. paternity가 disavowed되지 않아 natural child로 presumed되는 한 biological father가 혼인외 출생자로서 acknowledge할 수도 없고 child가 biological father를 상대로 action for acknowledgment를 제기할 수도 없으며, filing period가 지난 다음에는 그 presumption이 truth에 반하는 것으로 밝혀지더라도 overturn할 수 없다.
민법은 이와 같이 presumption of paternity provision과 이에 대한 rebuttal method인 provision on the action for disavowal of paternity를 strictly 정하고 있고, paternity를 disavow할 수 없게 된 경우 child’s legal status가 finally 확정된다. 따라서 혼인 중 출생한 child의 father-child relationship은 민법 provisions에 따라 uniformly determined되는 것이고 그 blood relationship을 individually and concretely examine하여 정해지는 것이 아니다. 즉, 민법은 혼인관계에서 출생한 child라는 fact에 근거하여 normatively parent-child relationship이라는 family relationship을 형성하고 그와 같이 formed family relationship에 strong legal protection을 부여한다. 이처럼 general and institutional aspects에서 child’s welfare를 보호하면서도 presumption of paternity provision에 따라 formed status relationship을 deny하고자 하는 사람에게는 reasonable method와 period를 정하여 status relationship에서 벗어날 수 있도록 함으로써 parent-child relationship determination을 둘러싸고 conflicting interests를 adjust하는 것이 민법의 basic attitude이다.
혼인 중 출생한 child에 대한 presumption of paternity의 standard를 어떻게 정할 것인가의 issue는 spouse와 child의 legal status와 related되는 것으로서 ‘법률적인 parent-child relationship을 truth에 coincide시키고자 하는 spouse·child의 interest’와 ‘parent-child relationship의 prompt determination을 통하여 legal stability를 찾고자 하는 child의 interest’를 social reality나 traditional conceptions에 맞게 어떻게 harmonize할 것인가에 관한 issue이다. 이는 interested parties의 fundamental rights, 혼인과 가족생활에 관한 constitutional decision을 고려하여 결정할 issue로서 원칙적으로 legislature의 discretion에 맡겨져 있다(헌법재판소 2015. 4. 30. 선고 2013헌마623 전원재판부 결정 참조). 민법은 presumption of paternity provision과 provision on the action for disavowal of paternity를 통하여 혼인 중 conception and birth한 child에 대한 parent-child relationship setting standard에 관한 legislative decision을 하였다고 볼 수 있다.
(나) 다음으로 presumption of paternity provision을 artificial insemination children에게도 equally apply해야 하는 reason에 관하여 본다.
law interpretation의 goal은 legal stability를 침해하지 않는 범위에서 concrete appropriateness를 pursue하는 데 있다. 이를 위하여 가능한 한 statute에 used된 text의 ordinary meaning에 faithful하게 interpret하는 것이 principle이지만, text의 ordinary meaning을 벗어나지 않는 범위에서는 law의 legislative purpose and object, enactment and amendment history, harmony with the legal order as a whole, 다른 laws and regulations과의 relation 등을 고려하는 systematic and logical interpretive methods를 additionally employ하여 law interpretation의 goal에 맞는 reasonable interpretation을 할 수 있다(대법원 2009. 4. 23. 선고 2006다81035 판결, 대법원 2014. 12. 11. 선고 2013므4591 판결, 대법원 2016. 11. 25. 선고 2015두37815 판결 등 참조). 그리고 입법 당시 contemplated하지 않은 phenomenon도 legislative solution이 없으면 existing legal system structure에 편입시켜 more reasonable solution을 도모하여야 한다.
presumption of paternity provision은 simply 아내가 혼인 중에 임신한 child를 husband’s child로 presume한다고 정하고 있을 뿐이다. text상 presumption of paternity provision은 conception이 된 specific circumstance에 따라 presumption의 application을 limit하거나 natural means가 아닌 artificial insemination으로 임신한 child에 대해서 presumption의 application을 exclude하지 않는다. 이러한 form의 presumption of paternity provision은 2017. 10. 31. Act No. 14965로 amended될 때에도 그대로 maintained되었다. 그 밖에 other provisions of the Civil Act를 보더라도 artificial insemination children에 대해서 presumption of paternity provision의 application을 exclude하거나 이를 restrict하지 않는다. 따라서 artificial insemination child에 presumption of paternity provision을 applying하는 것은 statutory text가 허용하는 interpretation의 scope 내에 있다.
헌법 제36조 제1항은 “혼인과 family life는 individual dignity와 equality of the sexes를 기초로 성립되고 유지되어야 하며, the State shall guarantee this.”라고 정하여 개인의 autonomous intent와 equality of the sexes에 기초한 marriage와 이를 바탕으로 formed family life를 protect하고 있다. presumption of paternity provision은 이러한 constitutional principles를 바탕으로 부부가 normal married life를 하고 있는 경우 이를 기초로 formed family relationships에 stable legal status를 부여하여 domestic peace를 유지하는 데에 기여한다. artificial insemination child가 birth하게 된 background인 marital relationship, 그리고 혼인 중 artificial insemination child가 birth함에 따라 발생하게 되는 parent-child relationship 등의 family relationships도 이처럼 respect받아야 할 individual과 family autonomy에 기초하여 formed 것이므로 other children born during marriage와 discriminate해서는 안 된다. 혼인을 바탕으로 formed family life에 대한 protection necessity는 혼인 중 출생한 child가 artificial insemination child라는 reason으로 달라지지 않는다. conception하게 된 specific circumstance에 따라 혼인 중 출생한 child에 대한 legal status가 달라진다고 볼 legal basis가 없다. normal marital relationship을 유지하고 있는 상태에서 출생한 artificial insemination child에 대해서 sexual intercourse에 의해 출생한 자가 아니라는 reason으로 presumption of paternity provision의 application을 exclude할 reasonable reason도 없다.
presumption of paternity provision은 혼인 중 출생한 child에게 birth와 동시에 stable legal status를 부여하여 legal protection의 gap을 없애고자 한 것이다. 이것은 혼인 중 artificial insemination으로 출생한 child에 대해서도 마찬가지이다.
sexual intercourse나 biological blood relationship만을 parent-child relationship formation의 basis로 삼거나 이를 reason으로 artificial insemination child가 husband’s child로 presumed될 수 없다고 보는 것은 혼인 중 출생한 artificial insemination child에 대해서 father를 정할 수 없는 state를 초래한다. 이는 artificial insemination child의 legal status를 unstable하게 함으로써 민법이 presumption of paternity provision을 두게 된 system purpose와 directly conflict되어 unjust하다. artificial insemination child에 대해서 presumption of paternity provision을 applying하지 않고 biological blood relationship만을 prioritize할 경우에는 더욱 unjust results를 초래한다. sperm donor가 anonymous인 경우에는 donor를 특정하기 어렵다. sperm donor는 자신의 sperm로 태어날 child에 대해서 father로서 책임져야 한다는 것을 예상할 수 없어 father role을 기대하기 어려울 뿐만 아니라, anonymously sperm를 제공한 것 외에 child의 conception and birth에 대해서 father로서의 status를 attribute할 만한 다른 role을 하지 않는다. 따라서 blood relationship이 있다는 fact만으로 sperm donor를 곧바로 legal father로 treat하거나 그에게 legal father로서의 responsibility를 묻는 것은 타당하지 않다. 이처럼 artificial insemination child에 대해서 presumption of paternity provision에 따라 father-child relationship을 정하지 않으면 사실상 father-child relationship을 정할 수 없게 되거나 민법이 예상하지 않은 father-child relationship이 성립하도록 하는 등 unjust results를 가져온다.
요컨대, presumption of paternity provision은 혼인 중 출생한 child에 대해서 적용되는데, presumption of paternity provision의 text와 legislative purpose, 혼인과 family life에 대한 constitutional guarantee 등에 비추어 혼인 중 출생한 artificial insemination child도 혼인 중 출생한 child에 포함된다고 보아야 한다.
(다) child’s welfare는 parent-child relationship의 formation and maintenance에서 가장 우선적으로 고려해야 할 사항이므로, artificial insemination child에 대해서 presumption of paternity provision이 적용되는지를 따질 때에도 child’s welfare에 중점을 두어야 한다. child’s welfare는 simply child에게 protection·upbringing의 guarantee라는 parent-child relationship의 substance를 제공하는 것에 국한하지 않고 이에 상응하는 legal parent-child relationship을 형성해 줌으로써 parents의 role을 할 수 있도록 해야 하고, 이에 따라 parents가 child’s development를 위한 support를 충분히 할 수 있도록 institutionally guarantee해 주어야 한다. child’s welfare를 continuously 책임지는 parent에게 child와의 status relation을 attribute하는 것이 child’s welfare에 도움이 된다. artificial insemination child에 대해서 natural parent-child relationship이 생기지 않는다고 보는 것은 artificial insemination child를 양육해 왔던 married couple에게 huge shock일 뿐만 아니라 이를 바탕으로 family relationship을 형성해 온 child에게도 irreversible risk라고 할 수 있다.
(라) artificial insemination child의 birth process와 이를 둘러싼 실제 family relationship의 모습에 비추어 보더라도 artificial insemination child에 대해서 presumption of paternity provision을 applying하는 것에 social appropriateness를 인정할 수 있다.
artificial insemination의 경우 natural sexual intercourse라는 element가 없는 대신 auxiliary act인 artificial insemination 또는 embryo transfer가 존재한다. 아내가 third party의 sperm를 통한 artificial insemination method로 child를 conceive하는 데에 남편이 consent하는 경우 부부는 artificial insemination child가 husband와 blood relationship이 없더라도 child에 대해서 jointly responsible한다는 것을 anticipated하였을 것이고 그 consent에 따라 출생한 child와 parent-child relationship을 form하게 된다고 보아야 한다. 남편은 아내가 artificial insemination으로 인한 conception과 childbirth를 하는 process에 consent함으로써 participate하게 되고 그 process에서 출생한 child는 부부 사이의 natural sexual intercourse로 conception·birth한 child와 마찬가지로 부부 사이에 혼인 중 출생한 child라고 볼 수 있다. 이러한 parent-child relationship을 바탕으로 artificial insemination child는 부부 사이의 child로서 그들과 substantive parent-child relationship의 모습을 form하고 maintain한다. socially로도 이와 같이 formed parent-child relationship은 natural sexual intercourse로 출생한 child의 경우와 마찬가지로 부부의 child로 받아들여지고 있다.
그런데도 presumption of paternity provision의 application을 exclude하거나 artificial insemination child에 대해서 부부와 legal parent-child relationship이 established되지 않는다고 한다면, 이는 legal stability와 peace를 깨뜨려 artificial insemination child를 legal protection이 없는 vacuum state로 만드는 것으로서 우리 사회에서 받아들이기 어렵다.
(2) artificial insemination child에 대한 disavowal of paternity 허용 여부
(가) 위에서 보았듯이 provision on the action for disavowal of paternity는 legal parent-child relationships을 truth에 부합시키고자 하는 interest를 위하여 마련되었다. 그러나 blood relationship이 없는 child가 출생하였다는 점이 밝혀진 경우에는 presumption of paternity provision application의 premise가 없어진 것으로 볼 수 있다. 이러한 경우 민법은 husband와 wife가 family life와 status relations에서 누려야 할 personality rights, rights to pursue happiness, and fundamental rights concerning marriage and family life based on individual dignity and equality of the sexes를 guarantee하기 위하여 이들에게 reasonable period 범위 내에서 action for disavowal of paternity를 제기할 수 있도록 하고 있다(헌법재판소 1997. 3. 27. 선고 95헌가14, 96헌가7 전원재판부 결정 등 참조).
presumption of paternity provision에 따라 artificial insemination child를 husband’s child로 presume하는 reason은 ‘consent’를 함으로써 conception·birth process에 participate한 부부 사이에 출생한 child에 대해서 presumption of paternity provision을 applying하는 것이 Constitution과 Civil Act를 비롯한 전체 family law system에 비추어 justified하다고 볼 수 있기 때문이다. artificial insemination child에 대해서 presumption of paternity provision을 applying하는 것은 혼인관계에 있는 부부의 family life와 status relationship을 guarantee해 주면서 free will에 따라 family relationships을 form하고 socially recognized family relationships의 substance를 legally guarantee해 주기 위한 것이다.
artificial insemination child를 conceive하여 출산하는 process에 비추어 볼 때, artificial insemination child가 husband와 wife의 sexual intercourse로 conception한 것이 아니고 이에 따라 child가 husband와 blood relationship이 없다는 점은 모두 artificial insemination child에 대해서 presumption of paternity provision을 applying할 때에 already considered한 matters로서, artificial insemination child가 출생할 당시 husband가 알고 있던 facts와 다르지 않다. 이러한 premise facts를 바탕으로 presumption of paternity provision을 통하여 artificial insemination child를 husband’s child로 presume하는 것은 husband가 family life와 status relations에서 누려야 할 personality rights, rights to pursue happiness, and fundamental rights concerning marriage and family life based on individual dignity and equality of the sexes를 guarantee하고 이를 realize해 주기 위한 것이다. 이에 반대로 husband에게 action for disavowal of paternity를 제기할 수 있도록 하는 것이 husband의 fundamental right라고 말할 수 없다.
action for disavowal of paternity는 natural sexual intercourse로 conception·birth한 child에 대해서 sexual intercourse process가 없다는 것과 이에 따라 biological blood relationship이 없다는 것을 requisite로 제기할 수 있다. artificial insemination child에 대해서도 위와 같은 requisites로 action for disavowal of paternity를 제기할 수 있다고 한다면 natural parent-child relationship은 biological blood ties로 determined된다는 것을 전제로 하는 것으로서 artificial insemination을 통한 parent-child relationship formation을 deny하는 결과가 된다. 이는 민법이 presumption of paternity provision과 provision on the action for disavowal of paternity를 두어 blood ties 이외의 other factors도 고려하여 natural parent-child relationship을 정하고자 한 purpose나 objective에 합치되지 않는다.
(나) normally married life를 하고 있는 spouses 사이에서 artificial insemination child가 birth하는 경우 husband는 consent의 way로 child의 conception and birth에 participate하게 되는데, 이것이 presumption of paternity provision이 applied되는 basis라고 할 수 있다. husband가 artificial insemination에 consent하였다가 나중에 이를 reverse하고 action for disavowal of paternity를 제기하는 것은 allowed되지 않는다. 나아가 artificial insemination consent와 related된 current legal system의 deficiencies, artificial insemination이 이루어지는 medical reality, 민법 제852조에서 친생자임을 승인한 자의 친생부인을 제한하고 있는 purpose 등에 비추어 이러한 consent가 명백히 밝혀지지 않았던 circumstance가 있다고 해서 곧바로 parent-child relationship이 denied된다거나 action for disavowal of paternity를 제기할 수 있다고 볼 것은 아니다.
